artifacts.summary: Gate 20 already passes (stale 71712B overage already fixed by tasks 620/634); recommends a deliberate headroom re-baseline. Corrects the gate 8/10 timeout claim to gate 10 (plus possibly 3/4), recommends a static timeout_s raise rather than a load-adaptive mechanism, and flags an unreconciled scope overlap with task 610.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's agent-system, orchestrator-context-budget.json's eager_load.baseline_bytes and the two per-file ceiling_bytes (commands/orchestrate.md, skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md) have been reactively bumped roughly 10 times since 2026-10-01, each landing with a 0-200B margin that the next ordinary edit re-trips. When gate 20 is found passing but history shows this pattern, prefer a deliberate headroom re-baseline (several hundred bytes of real slack) over hunting for more compaction -- recent entries already record 'no further redistributable bloat found nearby'.

verify-deploy.sh gate 10 (validate-state.sh --deep, timeout_s=60 in gate-registry.data) is a repeat false-positive under concurrent multi-dispatch CPU load on this host (24 cores): corroborated 3x on 2026-11-16 alone, always re-passing standalone in 61-66s. Gate 8's declared timeout_s is 1500 (not 60) and is serialized (runs alone) -- it is not part of this false-positive class despite sometimes being conflated with it in task descriptions. No load-adaptive timeout mechanism exists yet for individual gates; timeout_s is a static gate-registry.data field with no env-var override (unlike gate 8's own VERIFY_DEPLOY_GATE8_JOBS concurrency knob).
